free_tier.stated: Free search across file hosts: 'SearchFiles file search engine is a search tool which can search for information in files', with named engines for Mediafire, Keep2share/K2s, MediaFire and Mega.nz.
free_tier.notes: No query cap is published on the page read.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: an index of links, not a store of bytes

retention.stated: not applicable: the index lists links that live on the hosts

egress.terms: Downloads are served by the host behind each result, so the host's limits apply. SearchFiles itself transfers nothing.

interface_detail: Web search form with per-host engines. No API is published on the page read.
tooling: Browser only as read; a wrapper would have to scrape the result page.
chaining: The step before a debrid: find the link, then unrestrict it. Its value is the per-host engines (K2s, MediaFire, Mega) rather than a general web search, because each one indexes inside that host's file metadata.
limits_note: No rate limit, result cap or query budget is printed on the page read.
binding_note: SearchFiles stores and transfers nothing, so no byte constraint can bind. The first real limit is on the host a result points to.

identity_cost.detail: No account or login on the search form.

reliability_note: An index of other people's links inherits their rot: a result can point at a deleted file, and the index does not re-check on the way out.
confidence_note: The per-host engines and the free claim are read from the vendor page today. No query was run, so the index's real coverage is unmeasured.

evidence.proved: the per-host engines it advertises (Mediafire, Keep2share/K2s, MediaFire, Mega.nz) and the file-content search claim

notes: It is a search engine and not a provider of capacity; the debrid relevance is that it turns a host name into a link one can unrestrict.
